notes: Signatures for the simulated family Worm.Sim/7. Exact hashes are shown alongside behavioural markers on purpose: real AV engines use both, and hash-only detection is trivially defeated by a one-byte change.

families.name: Worm.Sim/7 (simulated)
families.notes: File infector that appends a marker to documents, clones itself into every folder it can write to, installs a run key plus a logon task, spreads over removable media, then replaces files with .locked blobs.

doubleExtension.explain: A file that claims to be a document but ends in an executable extension. The classic `Invoice.pdf.exe` trick — Windows hides the real extension by default.

ransomExtension.explain: An extension associated with mass-encryption payloads.

autorunInf.explain: autorun.inf on removable media: the mechanism that makes an infected USB stick run code on the next machine.

untrustedRunKey.explain: A logon entry pointing into AppData/Roaming or Temp instead of a signed program directory. Persistence hiding in user-writable space.

massClone.explain: The same file content appearing in many unrelated folders. Legitimate software does not usually do this; replicators do.

ransomNote.explain: The ransom note. Worth signature-matching separately: the note usually appears even when the encryption is only partly successful, and it is often the first thing a user reports.
